body: I don't think there will be a simple way to make inputs execute the conditional methods to accurately determine whether or not a field is required. I think our options are always yes or always no.
at least it works with 'create' and 'update'

Yeah. I don't think there is a clear cut approach to how we can handle custom functions. Defaulting to not required might be a good compromise. At least the browser won't incorrectly require possibly optional fields.

@MichalWadowski Are you creating a form for an existing record or a new one? 

I checked how required checks are being done, and I was totally wrong about custom methods not working before. Any custom callbacks defined on a validator are executed against the current form's entity. Unless your entity is not correctly aware of its new state the required attribute should be set correctly.
Interesting, I will try to reproduce this and get a fix done.

issue.body:
When reading non-existing entities after existing ones have been read, we should not re-use the previous context by accident. Instead a new blank entity should be used. This properly simulates the state of the missing entity, as it will be missing errors, and all attributes.

I also tried to add a test for #4792 but wasn't able to reproduce the error, so I'm waiting on some additional information.
